interpretation: Retorsion reading of the elenctic defence of non-contradiction. Demanding a demonstration of everything is lack of education (1006a5-11); but the principle can be shown elenctically if only the disputant says something (1006a11-13). Elenctic showing differs from demonstration: the demonstrator would seem to beg the question, whereas here the other party is responsible (1006a15-18). The starting point is not to ask him to say that something is or is not, but that he signify something to himself and another (1006a18-22); then something is already determinate, and the one responsible is the one who submits, for in doing away with speech he relies on speech (1006a24-26). The reading is methodological: it records Aristotle's strategy and is not formalized as a Lean proposition. The passage concerns non-contradiction, not excluded middle; IV.7 applies the same starting point to excluded middle (claim ARIST-MET-1012A-EXCLUDED-MIDDLE-ELENCTIC-A).
